Package com.societegenerale.failover.dashboard.metrics.source.sharedstore.jdbc

Class HeartbeatStoreJdbc

java.lang.Object
com.societegenerale.failover.dashboard.metrics.source.sharedstore.jdbc.HeartbeatStoreJdbc
All Implemented Interfaces:
HeartbeatStore
public class HeartbeatStoreJdbc extends Object implements HeartbeatStore
Durable HeartbeatStore backed by a single JDBC table — the store=jdbc counterpart to SnapshotStoreJdbc, so per-instance liveness survives a dashboard restart and, more importantly, stays consistent when the dashboard is embedded in multiple @Failover instances pointed at the same database: HeartbeatStoreInmemory is process-local, so each embedded dashboard would only ever see its own loopback heartbeat and show every peer as UNKNOWN. A shared table fixes that.

Table (INSTANCE_ID PK, LAST_SEEN TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE), named <tablePrefix> + BASE_TABLE (the prefix is validated — letters/digits/underscore only — since it is concatenated into SQL; use the same prefix as SnapshotStoreJdbc to namespace both tables together). LAST_SEEN is read/written as OffsetDateTime (always ZoneOffset.UTC) via setObject/getObject, converted to/from epoch-millis at this boundary so HeartbeatStore.lastSeen(java.lang.String) stays epoch-millis. The table is never created or altered by this store — schema management is the consuming service's responsibility; see the module docs for the DDL to run per dialect.

Fails soft. Unlike SnapshotStoreJdbc (the metrics path, which must fail loud — a broken store there is a broken dashboard), heartbeat is a supplementary liveness signal: a DataAccessException (e.g. the table doesn't exist because liveness.enabled was turned on without provisioning it first) is caught, logged once at WARN until the next successful call, and degrades to the same behaviour as no heartbeat ever received (lastSeen(java.lang.String) returns null → caller keeps LiveStatus.UNKNOWN; record(java.lang.String) silently drops the ping) — a misconfigured heartbeat table never breaks the dashboard or the ingest endpoint.

Anand Manissery

    • lastSeen

      public Long lastSeen(String instanceId)
      Description copied from interface: HeartbeatStore
      Returns the epoch-millis of the last recorded heartbeat for this instance, or null if no heartbeat has ever been received.

      A null return means heartbeat tracking is not active for this instance (the peer has not enabled it) — the instance keeps LiveStatus.UNKNOWN.
